transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-06-14
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alice Chen (Redwood AE), Marcos Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Linda Park (CISO, Cairnbridge), Omar Farid (Head of Ops), Jenna Liu (Legal), Samir Patel (Platform)

Summary (auto):
High-level discovery to map Cairnbridge Wealth's data residency constraints, incident evidence needs, and options for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment. Customer concerned about log retention, key residency, legal hold, and audit evidence for regulators. Asked for examples of encrypted key flows and redaction/workflow for Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in logs. Agreed next steps: security pack, architecture workshop, pilot + benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alice Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for joining the call, we've got about an hour. I'm Alice on the Redwood team, AE, and Marcos and Priya from our SE squad are here. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Linda Park: Hi Alice, thanks. Linda here — CISO. We got a few agenda items, main one is residency and audit trails for regulatory review, cause we get periodic exams.
[00:20] Omar Farid: Omar from Ops — we'll focus on the practical bits: where logs live, who can access keys, and the escalation path for incidents.
[00:29] Alice Chen: Great. Quick ask: are we scoped to financial regulator exams only or also cross-border privacy (GDPR)?
[00:36] Jenna Liu: We'll need both. We have customers in EU and US healthcare-adjacent plans, so GDPR plus HIPAA-adjacency are in scope for certain product lines.
[00:45] Marcos Diaz: Ok — thanks. To set context: Redwood supports three hosting modes — Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem). Each has different tradeoffs for data residency, key control, and evidence. We'll map those to your requirements.
[01:02] Samir Patel: Quick background — our infra is multi-region. For EU data we must keep logs and keys inside EU regions, and for some accounts we need keystore residency too. We're also under contractual legal hold obligations for 7 years in certain accounts.
[01:18] Priya Nair: Noted. Two immediate questions to help us recommend a path: 1) Do you need full control of KMS/HSM (customer-managed keys) or is a Redwood-managed KMS acceptable with residency guarantees? 2) How much raw telemetry/log detail do you need for audits vs what can be redacted?
[01:36] Linda Park: We need customer-managed keys for the high-risk accounts. For logs: auditors want request/response hashes and routing metadata, but we must redact PII before logs leave the customer's region.
[01:47] Alice Chen: Understood. Redwood Hosted can support region locking for EU requests, and we offer KMS integration for key wrapping, but in Hosted the ultimate KMS is Redwood-managed unless you adopt Dedicated or Private with a customer KMS.
[02:05] Marcos Diaz: Right — with Dedicated we can run dedicated GPU pools in a chosen region and integrate with your KMS via a peered HSM or external key manager; with Private deployment you run the control plane and keys entirely in your network. The cost and ops overhead increase along that path.
[02:24] Omar Farid: For audits we also need chain-of-custody for logs — we can't have vendor SREs able to read raw user data. How do you handle SRE access and support debug sessions?
[02:33] Priya Nair: We enforce role-based access; debug sessions can be done with redacted payloads and tied to specific runbooks. For Dedicated and Private, we can restrict SRE access further and provide time-limited access tokens and full audit trails. In Hosted, we have controls but not full removal of our operator role unless you choose Private.
[02:55] Jenna Liu: And in terms of legal hold, do you have exportable audit logs in an immutable format? Regulators often request tamper-evidence.
[03:04] Marcos Diaz: We can provide exportable readonly audit logs in parquet/csv with signatures. For Private, you can host the export target directly in your S3 or object store so evidence never leaves your jurisdiction. Hosted can replicate to region-locked buckets under Redwood's tenancy — we can provide attestations but not hand you the underlying storage control in all cases.
[03:28] Linda Park: Ok. A specific scenario — incident where a user data blob was processed and a regulator asks for the exact request, full KV cache traces, and decrypted context. Can you produce that without exposing other customers' data?
[03:42] Alice Chen: Short answer: yes, but with constraints. We keep per-tenant traces and can pull the request/response and the KV cache snapshots for that tenant. Redaction is applied for PII. Decrypting data would require access to the key; if your KMS is customer-managed, that decryption remains under your control.
[04:00] Samir Patel: So if we run Dedicated with our KMS, Redwood engineers won't be able to decrypt raw payloads, correct?
[04:06] Marcos Diaz: Correct — that setup preserves key residency and control. We would still have logs that say "decryption performed by customer KMS" as an event, but not the plaintext.
[04:17] Omar Farid: What's the typical log retention and cost impact for keeping request/response data for 7 years? That's a long time and we have to budget storage and retrieval costs for legal holds.
[04:29] Priya Nair: That's a good question. Most customers archive structured audit traces for the long term (hashes, metadata) and keep full request/response for a shorter operational window. For long legal holds, our recommendation is to snapshot the minimal evidentiary set and push to your cold archive — that's something we can automate in Dedicated/Private. We can share a cost model.
[04:51] Jenna Liu: On GDPR: cross-border transfers require documentation and controller-processor contracts. Does Redwood provide standard SCCs or DPA language?
[04:59] Alice Chen: Yes, we have a DPA and will supply SCCs where required; for Private deployments we'd also offer an enterprise contract amendment for residency guarantees. I'll attach our current DPA and SCC references.
[05:10] Linda Park: We need details on PII redaction at ingestion. Can you show an example of redaction rules and whether redaction happens before telemetry logging?
[05:20] Marcos Diaz: Redaction can be applied in two places: client-side (recommended) or server-side. Server-side redaction occurs before logs are written; we have regex and ML-based filters. Important caveat: server-side redaction relies on model inference which could have misses, so for high-risk fields we prefer client-side redaction or a dedicated ingest proxy in Dedicated/Private.
[05:44] Samir Patel: We currently have an ingest proxy layer. If we used Hosted, could we still send already-redacted payloads to Redwood?
[05:51] Priya Nair: Absolutely. We support sending masked payloads; that reduces the evidence available later, so if you need full raw for legal reasons you'd have to retain copies internally.
[06:05] Omar Farid: For forensic timelines, do you provide precise timestamps with timezone normalization and sequence IDs so we can correlate with our logs?
[06:13] Marcos Diaz: Yes — every event includes UTC timestamps, request IDs, and recovered sequence tokens where applicable. We can also integrate with your tracing system if you provide the trace IDs on inbound requests.
[06:26] Jenna Liu: A compliance-oriented question: do you undergo regular penetration tests and will you share summaries?
[06:32] Alice Chen: We do. We'll share executive summaries and remediation notes; full reports are available under NDA.
[06:40] Linda Park: Can you walk through a sample incident escalation? We need a runbook that maps Redwood notifications to our internal incident managers and regulatory timelines.
[06:49] Marcos Diaz: Sure. For production incidents that impact data residency or leakage, we do a "data-impact" assessment within 2 hours, notify designated contacts, provide initial evidence within 24 hours, and a full report in under 5 business days. For Private, timelines are faster since you control more of the surface. We'll share our standard incident runbook.
[07:10] Samir Patel: About SSO and RBAC — we use SAML + SCIM provisioning and strict separation between dev and prod accounts. Can Redwood integrate with our IdP and enforce least privilege?
[07:20] Priya Nair: Yes, we support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and custom RBAC roles. For Dedicated/Private we can map roles to your LDAP groups and ensure operator access is scoped.
[07:33] Omar Farid: For Dedicated there's sometimes the need for peering and network-level controls. Do you support private peering and single-tenant routing?
[07:41] Marcos Diaz: We do. Dedicated supports VPC peering, private links, and dedicated egress IPs. Private deployment gives you full network control. We'll capture Samir's network diagram and propose options.
[07:54] Linda Park: About data deletion and right to be forgotten — how does Redwood ensure deletion from caches and backups?
[08:02] Alice Chen: Deletion flows are different per hosting mode. Hosted: we mark and scrub caches and follow retention windows; backups are stored per our retention policy, and we can coordinate deletes. Dedicated/Private: you can control immediate purges. We'll share our deletion SLA and how we attest deletion to you.
[08:20] Jenna Liu: Another legal angle — regulators may request preserved logs under legal hold. We need sovereignty of those preserved copies. How would that work if we use Hosted?
[08:29] Marcos Diaz: For Hosted we can pin a preserved copy to a region-located archive and limit access. But final control still sits with Redwood for underlying storage unless you move to Dedicated/Private where you control the archive target.
[08:44] Samir Patel: Are there known performance or cost tradeoffs if we push for maximum residency (i.e., all EU traffic to run through EU-only pools)?
[08:53] Priya Nair: Slight latency improvements for regional routing but cost increases if we need dedicated capacity per region and fewer sharing opportunities. Our Optimize tooling can model expected cost per 1M tokens with regional isolation. We'll run that model for you.
[09:09] Linda Park: Ok, let's pivot to evidence formats. We need signed digests, exportable manifests, and a chain-of-custody record. Do you support signed manifests?
[09:18] Marcos Diaz: Yes — we can produce signed manifests (SHA-256 with server signature) and timestamp the export. For maximum assurance we can include a per-tenant signing key and cross-signed logs.
[09:31] Omar Farid: Will Redwood's SREs ever have root-level access to customer buckets in Dedicated?
[09:38] Alice Chen: In Dedicated we can arrange for restricted SRE access and require elevated access only via a documented and audited jump process. In Private, SREs have no access unless you onboard a support VPN.
[09:50] Jenna Liu: One more — encryption in transit and at rest. We need TLS mutual auth for critical paths; do you support mTLS to upstreams and control plane?
[09:59] Marcos Diaz: We support mTLS for peering and can terminate TLS at ingress per your preferences, and we support TLS 1.2/1.3. We'll include details in the security pack.
[10:10] Samir Patel: Regarding on-prem/private — what's included in the on-prem bundle? Do you ship a pre-built appliance image, and how is updates handled?
[10:18] Priya Nair: The on-prem bundle is a control plane VM + runtime containers. We provide a signed update channel; updates can be staged in a staging VPC and promoted. For air-gapped environments we provide a release artifact and signed checksums.
[10:33] Linda Park: For auditors, we need proof that updates were applied and that the image hasn't been tampered with. Will you provide update attestations?
[10:39] Marcos Diaz: Yes, signed release notes and checksums; for Private we can rotate keys and provide the attested update history as part of the evidence export.
[10:51] Alice Chen: Quick check: are there any non-negotiables that would force you to choose Private over Dedicated or Hosted?
[10:59] Linda Park: Customer-managed keys in our EU accounts and absolute prohibition on vendor access to plaintext are probably non-negotiable. Also, some legacy clients require on-prem processing.
[11:10] Omar Farid: And we prefer no raw request payloads leaving EU for those accounts.
[11:14] Alice Chen: Got it. That steers us toward Dedicated with your KMS or Private for certain accounts. We'll map which tenants need which mode.
[11:23] Marcos Diaz: We'll create a tenancy matrix: which product lines/tenants are EU-only, HIPAA-adjacent, or legacy on-prem. That will help sizing and cost.
[11:33] Priya Nair: Also worth noting — we can do hybrid. Some customers keep high-risk accounts on Private or Dedicated and use Hosted for lower-risk workloads to save cost.
[11:44] Samir Patel: About cost modeling: show us the delta for full tenancy isolation vs shared Dedicated pools. We need per-tenant TCO.
[11:54] Alice Chen: We'll deliver that. Marcos will prepare a 3-scenario cost projection: Hosted (region-locked), Dedicated (shared but isolated pools), Private (full control).
[12:05] Linda Park: For proof-of-concept, we'd like to see a redaction demo and an incident evidence extraction in a controlled environment. Can Redwood run that against a sample dataset?
[12:15] Marcos Diaz: Yes. Proposal: a 2-week POC using a sandbox tenant in Hosted or a small Dedicated slice where we demonstrate ingestion, redaction, exportable evidence, and runbook execution.
[12:27] Jenna Liu: Legal wants to review DPA before we spin up a test.
[12:31] Alice Chen: We'll send the DPA and SCCs.
[12:34] Omar Farid: Network-wise, we'll send you the peering diagram and IP allowlist.
[12:38] Samir Patel: We'll also share a list of top 10 fields that must be redacted.
[12:44] Priya Nair: Perfect — that gives us everything to scope the POC.
[12:49] Linda Park: A practical question: do you persist KV cache snapshots for auditing? If so, for how long and can we control it?
[12:58] Marcos Diaz: We persist ephemeral KV caches for performance and snapshots are not kept by default. For auditing we can snapshot on-demand and push to your archive. We don't keep long-term KV caches unless explicitly requested.
[13:12] Alice Chen: Before we wrap, let me restate the next steps so we're aligned. We'll: 1) send security pack (DPA, SOC2, ISO summary, signed manifest examples), 2) schedule architecture workshop with Samir and Priya, 3) propose a POC plan (sandbox or small Dedicated slice) and cost delta, 4) send a template runbook and evidence export sample.
[13:36] Linda Park: That sounds right. One ask — when you send the security pack, can you annotate which items are only available in Dedicated/Private?
[13:45] Alice Chen: Yes, we'll annotate feature availability by hosting mode.
[13:49] Jenna Liu: And please include the signed release attestation and penetration test executive summaries under NDA.
[13:55] Alice Chen: We'll include those and a link for NDA if needed.
[13:59] Omar Farid: Any quick concerns on our side? I think Samir will gather the infra diagrams.
[14:05] Samir Patel: I'll get those over. Also want to book a 90-minute architecture workshop next Tuesday if you have availability.
[14:12] Alice Chen: We can do next Tuesday, I'll propose times after the call. Marcos, Priya — anything to add?
[14:18] Marcos Diaz: I'll prepare the benchmark plan and evidence export examples.
[14:22] Priya Nair: And I'll draft the POC checklist and redaction demo steps.
[14:26] Alice Chen: Great. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with the pack and invites.
[14:31] Linda Park: Thanks.
[14:33] Jenna Liu: Thanks all.
[14:36] Meeting end.
